title: Old Grandmother Selling Betel Nut (Meirad Die Kwai)
cultural_context: Published historical Khasi song from authentic literature, documenting ancestral culture, moral philosophy, and oral tradition.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha rud ka surok I Mei-rad I shong,
Da ka shang ba dap da u kwai bad u tympew;
I khmied da ka khmat ba phuh samrkhie,
Ban ai ia u kwai ia ki nongleit nongwan.

'Wan shim ko khun ia u kwai uba thiang,
U kwai ba pyniasoh ia ka jingialok;'
Kumta I kren da ka ktien ba jemnud,
Kaba pynkmen ia ka mynsiem jong baroh.
lyrics_english:
Beside the village path sitting gently is the grandmother,
With her woven basket full of betel nut and fresh pepper leaves;
She gazes with smiling, welcoming eyes,
Offering the token of Kwai to every passing traveler.

'Come partake, my child, of the sweet fresh nut,
The Kwai that knits the bonds of brotherhood;'
Thus she speaks in tender gentle accents,
Cheering the weary spirits of all who pass by.
